beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. You leave a meeting with a notebook full of half-sentences, and three days later you cannot tell what anyone agreed to. The naive fix is to take better notes. But the better question is the one on screen.

show.event: types 'How do I take better meeting notes'
backspaces 'take better meeting notes' -> 'get Claude to turn the meeting into notes'

props.text: How do I take better meeting notes

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A transcript: the written record of what was said. A summary: the short version — what mattered. An action item: one task, one owner, one deadline.

beats.narration_text: Meetings are where decisions go to hide. Ninety minutes, eight people, four tangents about the coffee machine — and somewhere in there, a real decision about the launch date. Nobody writes it down. By Friday, three people remember three different versions.

shot.visual_intent: A long messy transcript page drops onto the stage, lines tangled; three small bubbles land above it, each remembering a different date. Label 'the meeting' beside the page.
shot.motion_claim: A long messy transcript page drops onto the stage, lines tangled; three small bubbles land above it, each remembering a different date. Label 'the meeting' beside the page.

beats.narration_text: The fix is simple. Paste the transcript — or your rough notes — into Claude. You hand it the mess; it hands back the meaning. No formatting, no clean-up needed first.

shot.visual_intent: The transcript page slides into the chat window's composer; a reply card grows beside it with a terracotta check. Labels 'mess in' and 'notes out'.
shot.motion_claim: The transcript page slides into the chat window's composer; a reply card grows beside it with a terracotta check. Labels 'mess in' and 'notes out'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: And you do not need a perfect transcript. Your video-call app probably transcribes for you already. Your own rough notes work too — paste the fragments as they are. Claude reads the sense, not the formatting.

shot.visual_intent: Three fragment cards ('launch??', 'Sam — paymt', 'release notes?') drop into the composer as-is; a check lands on the composer. Label 'rough notes' beside them.
shot.motion_claim: Three fragment cards ('launch??', 'Sam — paymt', 'release notes?') drop into the composer as-is; a check lands on the composer. Label 'rough notes' beside them.

beats.narration_text: The first prompt is: summarize this meeting in 3 bullets. Three, not ten — the limit forces it to pick what mattered. What you get is the whole meeting in about thirty seconds.

shot.visual_intent: The exact prompt sits in the composer; a reply grows with three bullet lines and terracotta dots. Label 'summarize' beside the reply.

beats.narration_text: The second prompt is: list every decision and who owns the next step. This is the one that matters most. Meetings feel productive because people talked. This prompt asks the uncomfortable question: who actually does what.

shot.visual_intent: The exact prompt lands in the composer in two lines; a reply card grows with two decision rows, each with an owner pill ('Maya', 'Sam'). Label 'owners' beside the reply.

beats.narration_text: The third prompt is the one most people skip: what was left unresolved? Every meeting leaves loose ends — the question nobody answered, the thing everyone nodded at but nobody owns. This prompt hunts them down.

beats.narration_text: Watch it work. Maya moves the launch to Friday, Sam owns the payment fix, and nobody decides who writes the release notes. Transcript in — summary, decisions, three action items out. And one unresolved question: who writes the release notes?

beats.narration_text: The notes are not the end. Keep asking. Draft the follow-up email to the team. Or: what should I prepare before next week's check-in? The transcript is now a document you can question.

beats.narration_text: One line of caution. Check your workplace rules before pasting an internal meeting into a public AI. If the rules say no, use your rough notes instead of the transcript.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here is the meeting transcript, pasted below. Give me three things: 1. a three-bullet summary. 2. every decision and who owns the next step. 3. what was left unresolved. Then check two things yourself. One: does every action item have a named owner? If one just says the team, ask Claude: who? Two: does the summary stay short? If it wanders, say: shorter.
